anchorData: SCHOOL AND TANK: Kilimani Secondary School, Nakuru. The steel-framed water tank tower has its top of tank 7.5 m above the ground (caretaker's tape-measured check value, revealed only in Lesson 8). Learners' eye height is 1.5 m for every learner, so the top of the tank is 7.5 − 1.5 = 6.0 m above eye level. Two learners sight the top of the tank with a protractor-and-string clinometer. WANJIRU stands 8 m from the base of the tower and reads an angle of elevation of 37°. Calculation: tan 37° = 0.7536; 8 × 0.7536 = 6.03 m above eye level; 6.03 + 1.5 = 7.53 m, which rounds to 7.5 m. OTIENO stands 10 m from the base and reads an angle of elevation of 31°. Calculation: tan 31° = 0.6009; 10 × 0.6009 = 6.01 m; 6.01 + 1.5 = 7.51 m, which rounds to 7.5 m. Wanjiru is closer (8 m < 10 m) and gets the larger angle (37° > 31°). Both get the same height of 7.5 m, which is the consistency check. Angles are read to the nearest degree and distances are measured with a tape along level ground. LESSON 2 TABLE (35° triangles, ideal measured values in cm, lengths to 1 d.p.): Triangle A: adjacent 4.0, opposite 2.8, hypotenuse 4.9, sin = 2.8/4.9 = 0.571, cos = 4.0/4.9 = 0.816, tan = 2.8/4.0 = 0.700. Triangle B: adjacent 8.0, opposite 5.6, hypotenuse 9.8, sin = 0.571, cos = 0.816, tan = 0.700. Triangle C: adjacent 12.0, opposite 8.4, hypotenuse 14.7, sin = 0.571, cos = 0.816, tan = 0.700. Real learner measurements will vary by about ±0.02. Calculator values for 35°: sin 35° = 0.5736, cos 35° = 0.8192, tan 35° = 0.7002. LESSON 3 TABLE (4 d.p.): 20° and 70°: sin 20° = 0.3420, cos 20° = 0.9397, sin 70° = 0.9397, cos 70° = 0.3420. 30° and 60°: sin 30° = 0.5000, cos 30° = 0.8660, sin 60° = 0.8660, cos 60° = 0.5000. 35° and 55°: sin 35° = 0.5736, cos 35° = 0.8192, sin 55° = 0.8192, cos 55° = 0.5736. 45° and 45°: sin 45° = cos 45° = 0.7071. LESSON 4 PRACTICE ANSWERS: (a) Kisumu roof rafter: the horizontal span from wall to centre is 3.6 m and the rafter makes 30° with the horizontal, so rafter = 3.6 ÷ cos 30° = 3.6 ÷ 0.8660 = 4.2 m (4.16 m). (b) Kericho stream: a learner stands on the bank directly opposite a tree on the far bank, walks 20 m along the bank, and the line of sight to the tree makes 40° with the bank, so the stream width = 20 × tan 40° = 20 × 0.8391 = 16.8 m. (c) Mombasa mango tree: 12 m from the base, elevation 28°, eye height 1.5 m, so height = 12 × tan 28° + 1.5 = 12 × 0.5317 + 1.5 = 6.38 + 1.5 = 7.9 m. (d) The water-tank calculation uses Wanjiru's data above. LESSON 5 CLINOMETER: a cardboard protractor, a straw taped along the straight edge, a string with a washer hung from the centre mark. Practice target: the top of the classroom door frame, 2.1 m high, sighted from 3.0 m away (eye 1.5 m), so the expected elevation is about 11° (tan⁻¹ of 0.6/3.0 = 0.2 gives 11.3°). Only the expected angle is given, not worked, since inverse ratios are not taught. LESSON 6 SAMPLE DATA: school flagpole, caretaker's tape height 9.0 m. Group Amani stands 15 m from the base and reads an elevation of 27°. Height = 15 × tan 27° + 1.5 = 15 × 0.5095 + 1.5 = 7.64 + 1.5 = 9.1 m. The error is 0.1 m, which comes from reading to the nearest degree. Angle of depression: from the veranda, eye level 3.0 m above the ground, to a ground marker 4.0 m from the veranda base, the depression is 37°. Check: tan 37° = 0.7536, 4.0 × 0.7536 = 3.01 m, which is about 3.0 m. LESSON 7 PROBLEM ANSWERS: (a) Rift Valley farmer at 150 m from the cliff base, elevation 40°, eye height ignored: height = 150 × tan 40° = 150 × 0.8391 = 125.9 m, about 126 m. (b) Watamu: a diver's weighted line is 12 m long and makes 50° with the horizontal surface, so depth = 12 × sin 50° = 12 × 0.7660 = 9.2 m. (c) Nairobi ramp: length 5 m along the slope at 8° to the horizontal, so rise = 5 × sin 8° = 5 × 0.1392 = 0.70 m (0.7 m).
characters: WANJIRU: Grade 10 learner at Kilimani Secondary School, Nakuru; stands 8 m from the tank tower; measures 37°. OTIENO: Grade 10 learner, Wanjiru's classmate; stands 10 m from the tower; measures 31°. MR. KAMAU: the school caretaker, who tape-measured the tank during a maintenance climb; the top of the tank is 7.5 m high; his figure is only revealed in Lesson 8. MADAM ACHIENG: the Essential Mathematics teacher. GROUP AMANI: outdoor group of 4 in Lesson 6; measures the flagpole. KILIMANI SECONDARY SCHOOL: Nakuru; has a steel-frame water tank tower and a flagpole 9.0 m tall. WATER TANK TOWER: top of tank 7.5 m above the ground, on a level concrete base. FLAGPOLE: 9.0 m tall, the same level ground. CLINOMETER: a class-made instrument of a cardboard protractor, a straw, a string and a washer. Other named contexts: Kisumu roof rafter, Kericho stream, Mombasa mango tree, Rift Valley farmer's cliff, Watamu diver, Nairobi ramp. Real-world links: surveyors in the Kenyan highlands, engineers on the Thika Superhighway, foresters in the Mau Forest.
outcome: Wanjiru (8 m, 37°) and Otieno (10 m, 31°) record different angles but both calculate a tank height of 7.5 m, using height = distance × tan(angle) + 1.5 m eye height. The method works because the ratio opposite ÷ adjacent depends only on the angle, not on the size of the triangle. In Lesson 8 learners use their own clinometer data to confirm the calculation, and Mr. Kamau's tape check of 7.5 m agrees within the rounding error of reading angles to the nearest degree.
conventions: The acute angle is called θ (theta), and the three sides are named from θ: hypotenuse (opposite the right angle, longest), opposite (across from θ), adjacent (next to θ, not the hypotenuse). Ratios: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent. Use the full names sine, cosine and tangent when first introduced, and the abbreviations sin, cos, tan afterwards; there is no SOH-CAH-TOA mnemonic before Lesson 2 and it may be used after Lesson 2. Calculators must be in degree (DEG) mode. Trig values are given to 4 decimal places, final lengths to 1 decimal place, with units m or cm. Angles are written in degrees with the ° symbol and to the nearest degree. Angle of elevation = the angle above the horizontal from the observer's eye up to the object. Angle of depression = the angle below the horizontal from the observer's eye down to the object. Angle of depression from A = angle of elevation from the lower point (alternate angles), as in the Lesson 6 veranda 37° example. Eye height is always 1.5 m, so for a clinometer measurement: height = (distance × tan angle) + 1.5 m. Clinometer reading: the string hangs against the protractor scale, and the angle of elevation is the number of degrees between the string and the 90° mark, which is when the straw is horizontal. The 'horizontal distance' is measured along level ground from the observer to the base of the object. Complementary angles sum to 90°. Inverse ratios (finding an angle) are NOT taught in this sub-strand; angles are given or read from the clinometer. Non-right-angled triangles (sine rule and cosine rule) are saved for a later lesson. Tank top height is 7.5 m, flagpole is 9.0 m, and these are never changed. The DQB has two columns, 'Questions' and 'Answered', plus a column for 'New understandings'.
